summary: Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and traditional teacher Huixian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi (1915–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Rissho University and was attested as a member at Kyoto University in 1967.

Jikidō Takasaki (1926–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University. His appointments included professor at the University of Tokyo and president of Tsurumi University.

Jim G. Shaffer (born 1944) is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He earned his BA at Arizona State University and PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (~1972–2010).

Jim Rheingans works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hamburg and completed his PhD at the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.
Jim Taylor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Macquarie University in 1989 and was attested in 2014 as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide.

Jin Y. Park is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jinah Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and has held posts at Vanderbilt University, the Institute for Advanced Study, and Harvard University.

Jinbo Shi (born 1940) specializes in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, where he later became Professor and Fellow emeritus.
Jinchuan Wan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2010, he was attested as a professor at both National Central University and Fo Guang University.
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. At The University of Hong Kong, he was attested in 2006 and served as Director (attested 2009–2010).

Jing-shen Tao (born 1933) is a historian and sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University (PhD ~1965–1969), and later served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).
Jingru Wang (1903–1990) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1928–1932) and held a post at Minzu University of China (~1952–1958).

Jinhua Chen is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki. He has held faculty posts at the University of Virginia and the University of British Columbia.

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Colorado and has held positions at City University of Hong Kong, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and Harvard University.
Jinling He is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Jinshi Fan (born 1938) is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University under Su Bai. She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and as a part-time professor at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as deputy director of history at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and as a researcher and professor at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe (1883–1959) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He held posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).
